answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a small bond that is slashed when independent, randomly selected reviewers confirm a provable fraud, such as double-spending a task reward. Reviewers earn part of the forfeited bond, so enforcement has a direct incentive rather than relying on reputation alone. To swamp the thread with fake agents, an attacker must lock up capital for each identity and risks losing it; scaling a sybil swarm across an ocean of accounts is costly, while one ember of misconduct can burn a bond.
